## python/carnot/verify/beaver_lite.py

**Verdict:** `DISHONEST_NAMING`

## VERDICT
DISHONEST_NAMING

## CLAIMS
“BEAVER-lite probability-mass certificates for arithmetic answer constraints.”  
“llama.cpp logits-backed top-K prefix enumerator.”  
“Enumerate prefixes and bound unsafe probability mass for final answers.”  
“Return empirical and BEAVER-lite probability-mass violation bounds.”

## IMPLEMENTATION_REALITY
The optional live path genuinely invokes `llama_cpp.Llama`, evaluates logits, and performs beam search; otherwise it explicitly uses deterministic fabricated completions with mock logprobs. However, it sums only the unsafe mass found in the truncated top-K frontier, ignores all omitted probability mass, and forcibly treats unfinished beams as terminal, so the reported value is not a valid upper bound.

## CLAIM_VS_REALITY_GAP
OUTRIGHT_FAKE

## GAMING_PATTERNS
none

## RECOMMENDATION
REIMPLEMENT_PROPERLY

## RATIONALE
The model integration is real and the mock fallback is honestly labeled, but the central “certificate” claim is mathematically false. Enumerated unsafe mass is generally a lower bound on total unsafe mass unless unexplored mass is conservatively included; calling it an upper bound makes this verifier unsuitable for production or headline results.
